results.title: A transformative year for Canva: 2025 in review
results.content: 2025 marked one year of Canva Enterprise⁠(opens in a new tab or window), and we were grateful to see global teams continue to adopt Canva as a simpler, more collaborative way to communicate visually at scale. Today, Canva is used by 95% of the Fortune 500, and customers like Docusign⁠(opens in a new tab or window) shared encouraging signs of impact, including time saved, stronger consistency, and more engaging content across their teams. These outcomes reflected a broader shift we’re seeing in [...] 2025 was a year where everything moved faster: creativity, AI, and the way people learn and work. Through all that change, our community kept growing and kept pushing us to think bigger about how Canva can help people achieve their goals. Across our team, our product, and our global community, this year brought moments that reminded us why we started Canva in the first place, and why the best chapters are still ahead. We’re excited to share a few highlights from the year, and even more excited [...] One of the defining moments of 2025 was the introduction of our Creative Operating System⁠(opens in a new tab or window), the biggest product launch in our history. Built for what we’re calling the Imagination Era, it introduced a fully connected, AI-powered foundation across the Visual Suite, making it easier for anyone to move from an idea to a finished design in seconds.

results.title: Canva AI 2.0 Turns the Design Platform Into an Agentic Creative System
results.content:
Canva has accelerated its transformation from a design tool into a full-stack marketing platform through product launches and acquisitions spanning late 2025 through April 2026. In October 2025, the company unveiled its Creative Operating System — introducing upgraded video tools, a marketing engine called Canva Grow and a new Canva Business tier. By year-end 2025, Canva reported $4 billion in ARR, 265 million monthly active users and 31 million paid subscribers. [...] On April 15, Canva launched Canva AI 2.0, which the company called its most significant product update since its debut. The release is available as a research preview, according to company officials.

It is powered by what Canva calls the Canva Design Model — a foundation model the company claims was built to understand the structure, hierarchy and complexity of real-world design. Canva said the model generates fully layered, editable output from a single prompt. [...] The AI 2.0 announcement lands on the heels of Canva's five acquisitions in the first quarter of 2026, including Simtheory (agentic AI and multi-model collaboration) and Ortto (customer data platform and marketing automation) and Ortto (customer data platform and marketing automation)"), both announced April 9. Canva has also brought in MagicBrief, MangoAI, Doohly, and Cavalry in the same period — a pace that signals the company is assembling infrastructure for a full marketing and content

results.title: Cyberattack on Canvas system causes chaos for students at thousands of schools | AP News
results.content:
The student newspaper at Harvard reported that the system there was down as well. Students at Johns Hopkins University simply got an error message when trying to view their final grades on the platform Thursday. And public school districts also sought to reassure parents, with officials in Spokane, Washington, writing that they aren’t “aware of any sensitive data contained in this breach.” [...] Virginia Tech acknowledged in a notice to students that the administration was aware of the effect on final exams and other end-of-semester activities. The University of New Mexico sent a similar message to the campus community, and the University of Florida urged students to stay alert for any phishing messages that appear to be from Canvas.

Teachers say they are having to find workarounds to help students study for exams and submit final assignments. [...] Canvas is used to manage grades, course notes, assignments, lecture videos and more. The hacking group posted online that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, with billions of private messages and other records accessed, Connolly said.

Students quickly took to social media to ask if others were unable to access Canvas, with many panicking that they could no longer view course materials housed within the platform to study for their final exams.
